threats.title: T13: Customers not told documents are AI-processed
threats.description:
The upload journey has no notice of AI processing or transfer to a third party.

Ref: DOC1 gap; DOC1 §3.1 p.6
Frameworks: LINDDUN U
Questions: Q3
threats.mitigation:
Privacy notice and consent text at upload; record the notice version accepted.

Architecture improvement: R6

threats.title: T5: Long-lived customer session tokens
threats.description:
A stolen session token remains usable for up to 24 hours with no stated revocation.

Ref: DOC1 §3.1 p.6
Evidence: "receive a session token valid for 24 hours"
Frameworks: API2:2023; A07:2025
threats.mitigation:
Short-lived access tokens with refresh rotation, revocation on logout and password change, MFA for account changes.

Architecture improvement: R7

threats.title: T4: Any file type accepted without content checks
threats.description:
An attacker can upload weaponised or malformed files that are passed to parsers downstream.

Ref: DOC1 §3.4 p.7
Evidence: "The Intake Service accepts any file type up to 100 MB"
Frameworks: A05:2025; A10:2025; CWE-434
threats.mitigation:
Allow-list file types, enforce size limits, AV/CDR scan before any parsing, fail closed on errors.

Architecture improvement: R2

threats.title: T2: Indirect prompt injection via uploaded documents
threats.description:
An attacker who uploads a crafted document can inject instructions that the summariser follows, and the summariser can write to the Case DB.

Ref: DOC1 §4.1 p.9 Table 4
Evidence: "Calls the LLM and executes the tool calls it requests"
Frameworks: LLM01:2026; ASI01
Refined by: T14, T15
threats.mitigation:
Treat document text as untrusted data and constrain what the agent can do (see child threats T14, T15).

Architecture improvement: R1

threats.title: T12: Reviewers approve summaries without seeing sources
threats.description:
Reviewers see only the AI summary, so incorrect or manipulated summaries can be approved into the case record.

Ref: DOC1 §4.6 p.14
Evidence: "sign in to the Review Portal with Entra ID SSO and approve the summary"
Frameworks: ASI09; LLM07:2026
threats.mitigation:
Show source citations next to the summary; require reviewer attestation; sample QA.

Architecture improvement: R8

threats.title: T6: Guessable document paths
threats.description:
Blob paths use sequential case numbers, so any path that accepts a case number could expose another customer's documents.

Ref: DOC1 §5.2 p.17
Evidence: "Blob paths use the sequential case number"
Frameworks: A01:2025; API1:2023; LINDDUN DD
threats.mitigation:
Random object keys, per-request ownership checks, SAS tokens scoped to one object with short expiry.

Architecture improvement: R5

threats.title: T10: No audit trail for case changes
threats.description:
There is no record of who changed a case or approved an AI summary, including changes made by the agent.

Ref: DOC1 gap; DOC1 §4.6 p.14
Frameworks: A09:2025; LINDDUN NR
Questions: Q2
threats.mitigation:
Append-only audit log capturing user and agent identity for every case change.

Architecture improvement: R8

threats.title: T8: Single shared vector index for all customers
threats.description:
Retrieval for one case can surface another customer's content because the index is not partitioned.

Ref: DOC1 §4.5 p.13
Evidence: "embedded into a single shared vector index"
Frameworks: LLM09:2026; LINDDUN L
Refined by: T17
threats.mitigation:
Per-tenant namespaces with filters enforced server-side, not in the prompt.

Architecture improvement: R5

threats.title: T7: Untrusted pull requests can influence the pipeline
threats.description:
PR builds share runners and secrets with main-branch builds, and third-party actions are unpinned.

Ref: DOC2 §2.1 p.4
Evidence: "PR builds run on the shared self-hosted runners used for main-branch builds"
Frameworks: CICD-SEC-4; A03:2025
Refined by: T21, T24
threats.mitigation:
Separate the untrusted PR path from the trusted build and deploy path (see child threats T21, T24).

Architecture improvement: R3

threats.title: T1: Customer documents sent to third-party LLM
threats.description:
Full document text, including personal data, leaves the tenant for the hosted LLM API; the design states no data processing terms, region or retention settings.

Ref: DOC1 §4.3 p.11
Evidence: "The prompt and full document text are sent to the hosted LLM API"
Frameworks: LLM02:2026; LINDDUN DD; LINDDUN NC
Questions: Q4
threats.mitigation:
Use an enterprise endpoint with zero data retention and region pinning under a DPA; redact personal data before the prompt; complete a DPIA.

Architecture improvement: R6

threats.title: T11: No limit on document length sent to the model
threats.description:
Large or adversarial uploads drive token cost and throttling of the LLM service.

Ref: DOC1 §4.3 p.11
Evidence: "There is no limit on document length"
Frameworks: LLM06:2026; API4:2023
threats.mitigation:
Per-tenant quotas, maximum tokens per job, circuit breaker on spend.

Architecture improvement: R6

labelText.text: F9: Review UI, Entra ID SSO

data.name: F9: Review UI, Entra ID SSO

threats.title: T9: Review Portal database connection not specified
threats.description:
The design does not say how the Review Portal authenticates to the Case DB or whether TLS is enforced.

Ref: DOC1 gap; DOC1 §4.6 p.14
Frameworks: A04:2025
Questions: Q1
threats.mitigation: Managed identity, TLS 1.2+, least-privilege stored procedures.

threats.title: T3: Cluster-admin credential used for deployment
threats.description:
Anyone who compromises a pipeline job can reuse the cluster-admin kubeconfig to take full control of the production cluster.

Ref: DOC2 §3.2 p.8
Evidence: "uses a cluster-admin kubeconfig stored as a repository secret"
Frameworks: CICD-SEC-6; CICD-SEC-5; A08:2025
Refined by: T22
threats.mitigation:
Workload identity federation (OIDC) with a namespace-scoped deploy role; no static credentials in CI.

Architecture improvement: R3

threats.title: T16: Parsers share a container with the orchestrator
threats.description:
A parser or OCR exploit in a crafted file gains the orchestrator's credentials and network access.

Ref: DOC1 §4.2 p.10
Evidence: "runs in the same container as the Agent Orchestrator"
Frameworks: A03:2025; A10:2025
Related: T4
threats.mitigation:
Run extraction in a separate sandboxed container with no credentials and no egress; patch parsing libraries from a curated repository.

Architecture improvement: R2

data.name: P3.2: Prompt Builder
data.description: Ref: DOC1 §4.1 p.9 Table 4; DOC1 §4.3 p.11

threats.title: T14: Untrusted document text mixed into the system prompt
threats.description:
The Prompt Builder concatenates the system prompt, document text and retrieved chunks with no separation, so injected text is read as instructions.

Ref: DOC1 §4.3 p.11
Evidence: "concatenates the system prompt, document text and top-5 retrieved chunks into one prompt"
Frameworks: LLM01:2026; ASI01
Refines: T2
threats.mitigation:
Spotlighting: wrap untrusted text in delimiters with an explicit data-only instruction; keep system prompt separate; strip instruction-like content.

Architecture improvement: R2

data.name: P3.3: Agent Orchestrator [see L2-P3.3]
data.description: Ref: DOC1 §4.1 p.9 Table 4; DOC1 §4.4 p.12

threats.title: T15: Agent executes write tools with service credentials
threats.description:
Any instruction the model follows can call update_case using the service's database credentials, with no user context or approval.

Ref: DOC1 §4.4 p.12
Evidence: "Tool calls are executed with the service's database credentials"
Frameworks: LLM03:2026; ASI02; ASI03
Refines: T2
Refined by: T26, T27, T28
threats.mitigation:
Least agency: read-only tools by default; writes become proposals approved in the Review Portal; user-scoped tokens for tool calls (see T26-T28).

Architecture improvement: R1

threats.title: T19: Validator checks format only
threats.description:
The Response Validator checks the JSON schema but not whether the content is grounded or safe to write.

Ref: DOC1 §4.1 p.9 Table 4
Evidence: "Checks the summary against the JSON schema"
Frameworks: LLM10:2026; LLM07:2026
Related: T12
threats.mitigation:
Add grounding checks against source text and block outputs containing instructions or links before writing.

Architecture improvement: R8

threats.title: T20: Conversation cache holds document content for 7 days
threats.description:
Redis keeps prompts and outputs containing personal data for 7 days with no stated encryption or access control.

Ref: DOC1 §4.4 p.12
Evidence: "Conversation state is cached in Redis for 7 days"
Frameworks: LLM02:2026; LINDDUN DD
Refined by: T29
Questions: Q5
threats.mitigation:
Minimise cached content, 24-hour TTL, Redis AUTH with TLS, private endpoint.

Architecture improvement: R5

data.name: P3.F4: Query top-5 chunks
data.description: Ref: DOC1 §4.3 p.11; DOC1 §4.5 p.13 | refines F7

threats.title: T17: Retrieval query has no tenant filter
threats.description:
Top-5 retrieval runs across the shared index, so chunks from other customers' documents enter the prompt.

Ref: DOC1 §4.3 p.11; DOC1 §4.5 p.13
Evidence: "top-5 retrieved chunks" | "single shared vector index"
Frameworks: LLM09:2026; A01:2025; LINDDUN DD
Refines: T8
threats.mitigation:
Server-side tenant filter on every query; per-tenant namespaces.

Architecture improvement: R5

threats.title: T18: LLM API key held in an environment variable
threats.description:
The API key can be read by anything running in the pod, including a compromised parser, and reused to impersonate the service.

Ref: DOC1 §4.3 p.11
Evidence: "using an API key stored in an environment variable"
Frameworks: A07:2025; LLM04:2026
Related: T16
threats.mitigation:
Managed identity or Key Vault reference with rotation; separate key per environment; egress restricted to the LLM endpoint.

Architecture improvement: R6

threats.title: T24: Third-party actions referenced by mutable tags
threats.description:
A compromised or re-tagged marketplace action runs with pipeline privileges.

Ref: DOC2 §2.3 p.5
Evidence: "Workflows reference marketplace actions by tag"
Frameworks: CICD-SEC-3; CICD-SEC-8; A03:2025
Refines: T7
threats.mitigation:
Pin actions by full commit SHA; allow-list approved actions; automated update PRs.

Architecture improvement: R3

threats.title: T23: Images deployed without signature verification
threats.description:
A tampered or substituted image in the registry is deployed to production without detection.

Ref: DOC2 §3.2 p.8
Evidence: "Image signatures are not verified at deployment"
Frameworks: CICD-SEC-9; A08:2025
Related: T3
threats.mitigation:
Sign images at build (Sigstore or Notation) with SLSA provenance; admission policy in AKS rejects unsigned images.

Architecture improvement: R4

data.name: P5.F4: Secrets exposed to PR jobs

threats.title: T21: Repository secrets exposed to pull request jobs
threats.description:
Code from a pull request runs on shared runners with access to repository secrets, including the deploy credential.

Ref: DOC2 §2.1 p.4
Evidence: "with access to repository secrets"
Frameworks: CICD-SEC-4; CICD-SEC-5; CICD-SEC-6
Refines: T7
Questions: Q6
threats.mitigation:
No secrets for PR workflows; ephemeral isolated runners for untrusted code; environment protection rules for secrets.

Architecture improvement: R3

threats.title: T25: Static service principal secret for the registry
threats.description:
A long-lived secret for pushing images can be stolen from the runner and used to push malicious images.

Ref: DOC2 §3.1 p.7
Evidence: "pushes them to Azure Container Registry using a service principal secret"
Frameworks: CICD-SEC-6
threats.mitigation:
OIDC federation for ACR push; scoped push-only role.

Architecture improvement: R3

threats.title: T22: Cluster-admin kubeconfig stored as a repository secret
threats.description:
A static cluster-admin credential in repository secrets gives full cluster control to anyone who can read secrets.

Ref: DOC2 §3.2 p.8
Evidence: "uses a cluster-admin kubeconfig stored as a repository secret"
Frameworks: CICD-SEC-6; CICD-SEC-5
Refines: T3
threats.mitigation:
OIDC federation to a namespace-scoped deploy identity; remove the kubeconfig secret.

Architecture improvement: R3

threats.title: T27: Tool router executes model requests without validation
threats.description:
Tool names and parameters from model output are executed as given, with no allow-list or parameter validation.

Ref: DOC1 §4.1 p.9 Table 4
Evidence: "executes the tool calls it requests"
Frameworks: ASI02; LLM10:2026
Refines: T15
threats.mitigation:
Allow-list tools per job type; schema-validate and bound every parameter; log every tool call with the job ID.

Architecture improvement: R1

threats.title: T28: search_cases is not scoped to the customer
threats.description:
Injected instructions can make the model search and summarise other customers' cases.

Ref: DOC1 §4.4 p.12
Evidence: "search_cases (reads the Case DB)"
Frameworks: ASI03; A01:2025; LLM02:2026; LINDDUN DD
Refines: T15
Related: T17
threats.mitigation:
Scope search_cases to the current customer using a user-scoped token or row-level security.

Architecture improvement: R1

threats.title: T26: update_case can change any case without approval
threats.description:
The model can set any case's status and summary, with no check that the case belongs to the current job and no human approval.

Ref: DOC1 §4.4 p.12
Evidence: "update_case (writes case status and summary)"
Frameworks: ASI02; ASI03; LLM03:2026
Refines: T15
threats.mitigation:
Replace with propose_case_update limited to the current case ID; the reviewer approves in the Review Portal.

Architecture improvement: R1

threats.title: T29: Tool results persisted in conversation memory
threats.description:
Results from search_cases, possibly other customers' data, are stored in the cache and reused in later prompts.

Ref: DOC1 §4.4 p.12
Evidence: "Conversation state is cached in Redis for 7 days"
Frameworks: ASI06; LLM02:2026; LINDDUN DD; LINDDUN L
Refines: T20
Questions: Q5
threats.mitigation:
Do not persist tool results; partition memory per case; 24-hour TTL.

Architecture improvement: R5
